title: GRPO Plus (v0.50.0)
description: GRPO Plus in Soup CLI v0.50.0 (live loss kernels v0.53.11). All 7 GRPO variants (standard/gspo/dapo/dr_grpo/bnpo/two_sided/rft) ship real math kernels, grpo_delta two-sided clipping, grpo_fp16 routing and task: prm live with per-step MSE, and since v0.76.0 every non-standard variant applies the grpo_beta KL penalty. Of the rollout backends only openenv runs (art, ruler and nemo_gym are accepted names that are not wired); long_context_grpo and vision_grpo wired nothing and are refused at load since v0.77.0 when set; reward_fn: judge_rank (v0.77.0) ranks each prompt's completions with an LLM judge you configure; and the stability keys behind GRPOStabilityCallback mostly record counters rather than change training.

headings.title: The KL penalty: every variant applies grpo_beta (v0.76.0)

blocks.html:
GRPO Plus (v0.50.0)

22 features. Unsloth + axolotl GRPO parity.

7 GRPO variants

blocks.code:
task: grpo
training:
  grpo_variant: gspo   # standard | gspo | dapo | dr_grpo | bnpo | two_sided | rft
  grpo_delta: 0.5      # required for two_sided, optional for gspo (clip radius,
                       # default 0.2). (0, 1]. Rejected on every other variant
  grpo_fp16: true      # explicit FP16 mixed precision

blocks.html:
The KL penalty: every variant applies grpo_beta (v0.76.0)

gspo, dapo, dr_grpo, bnpo, two_sided and rft train with a KL penalty of training.grpo_beta (default 0.1) against the reference policy (#1232). Each variant adds trl 0.29's per-token estimator exp(ref - logp) - (ref - logp) - 1, weighted by grpo_beta, to its per-token loss before its own reduction; rft applies it only to the completions it accepts and trains on. On a real trainer, the dapo loss and gradient equal trl's stock dapo ones at beta 0.1, 1 and 10 on the same generated batch. No speed or quality effect of the penalty is claimed.

(Since closed in v0.76.0: through v0.75.2 these variants validated grpo_beta and dropped it. The variant loss replaces trl's _compute_loss, the one place trl adds the KL term on Soup's path, so neither grpo_beta nor the beta the reward-hack controller sets at runtime changed the loss or the gradient, while trl still ran the reference forward on every step.) A variant config from v0.75.x trained with no KL term, and a v0.76.0 run of the same config will not reproduce it. If a recipe relied on the old behaviour (a dapo or dr_grpo recipe that expects to be KL-free), set grpo_beta: 0 explicitly.

  • grpo_beta: 0 is valid (#1247). It turns the KL penalty off, as the KL-free DAPO and Dr. GRPO recipes do, and it skips the reference-model forward pass. It is refused together with reward_hack_mitigation: kl_control or pid_lagrangian, because the controller needs a positive beta to steer: grpo_beta: 0 is mutually exclusive with reward_hack_mitigation='kl_control' (the mitigation controller requires a positive beta to steer); use grpo_beta > 0 or disable mitigation. A boolean or NaN grpo_beta is refused.
  • The kl metric is logged again for a variant with a non-zero grpo_beta, as trl's stock loss does: the masked batch mean of the per-token KL, averaged over the accepted tokens for rft (#1263).
  • Ratios are clamped before exponentiation (#1609). The kernels bound the importance ratio and the sequence ratio from above with a bound that adapts to the advantage's magnitude, and mask padding with a boolean mask, so a diverging policy no longer turns infinite terms into NaN parameter gradients. A run that went to NaN under a non-standard grpo_variant before v0.76.0 may have hit this.
  • Non-finite steps are skipped, for every task: grpo run (#342). A gradient watchdog zeroes non-finite gradients before the optimizer step, so that step updates nothing and the adapter is preserved. The step still counts toward the step total and the learning-rate schedule. The skipped-step count and fraction are saved in trainer_state.json, a run that skipped 5% or more of its steps prints a Gradient watchdog: warning at the end, and soup adapters audit reports the figure. Since v0.77.0 each skipped step's warning names how many parameters went non-finite and the first three of them, and trainer_state.json keeps the count and the first five names per step and for the run (nan_param_count, nan_param_names) (#2060).
  • Validation. task: grpo does not evaluate by default and does not hold data.val_split out of training: the split is ignored, every row trains, and the run prints a one-line note saying so. Set training.eval_steps to hold the split out and evaluate it; the validation number is then the held-out reward, eval_reward (#1223, #1389). See Training methods.
  • Gold answers. reward_fn: accuracy and the verifiable math domain now read the gold the way they read the completion, and a gold that states no single final answer is refused before generation. See RLVR.

Re-run this

If you trainedWhat was wrongWhat to do
task: grpo with grpo_variant other than standardThe variant dropped grpo_beta, so it trained with no KL term while trl still ran the reference forward each step (#1232). With reward_hack_mitigation, the controller moved a beta the loss ignoredRe-run if you need the KL-regularised behaviour. Set grpo_beta: 0 to keep the KL-free behaviour on purpose
task: grpo with grpo_variant other than standard, and a run that went to NaNImportance ratios were exponentiated without a bound, so a diverging policy could produce infinite terms and NaN gradients (#1609)Re-run. v0.76.0 clamps the ratio
task: grpo resumed with --resume, before v0.77.0Upstream: --resume "restored the optimizer and the step counter and trained a freshly initialised adapter" (#1768, #1797). grpo with grpo_beta: 0 writes no reference adapter and was not affectedUpstream: "Re-run any dpo, ipo or grpo training that was resumed from a checkpoint."
task: grpo with grpo_beta above 0 and training.relora_steps, on v0.76.0 or v0.76.1Every ReLoRA restart merged the trained adapter into the base weights trl reads the reference from, "so from the first restart on the reference was the policy as of that step, without an error" (#1835, #1891). Refused at config load since v0.77.0Re-run without relora_steps, or with grpo_beta: 0, which keeps ReLoRA
task: grpo with reward_fn: accuracy, or reward_fn: verifiable with verifiable_domain: mathSee RLVR: the gold was compared raw, and accuracy paid 0.5 for a gold that merely appeared in the completionRe-run if the logged reward sat near 0.0

LLM judge ranking reward: judge_rank (v0.77.0)

For a task with no checkable answer, reward_fn: judge_rank asks an LLM judge to compare each prompt's completions with each other (#2047, #2117, by @ybai08). GRPO compares completions only within one prompt's group, so one judge call sees all num_generations completions of a prompt and scores each from 0 to 1 against the others, in a fresh order on every call (seeded from training.seed). It also runs in an ensemble, such as reward_fn: "format,judge_rank". Where an answer can be checked, a rule-based reward (accuracy, verifiable, a .py file) is cheaper.

blocks.code:
task: grpo
training:
  reward_fn: judge_rank
  grpo_judge: "ollama://llama3.1"   # or https://host/model, http://localhost:8000/model
  grpo_judge_max_calls: 20000       # required, no default
  gradient_checkpointing: true

blocks.html:
Optional: grpo_judge_rubric (a file under the working directory; only each criterion's name and description are used, and without one the judge uses Soup's default criteria), grpo_judge_max_tokens (the judge's reply budget per call) and grpo_judge_max_failure_rate (the share of failed groups the run tolerates).

  • It sends your data out. Every prompt and every completion goes to the judge host you configure. grpo_judge takes a judge URL (ollama://<model>, https://host/model, or http:// to a loopback host) and is checked when the config loads: plain http only to a loopback host, and no private, link-local or reserved IP literal (see private addresses refused). (training.online_dpo_judge refuses such an IP literal at load too, and checks plain http later, at trainer setup.) Judge replies are bounded to 1 MiB.
  • It has a cost ceiling, and you have to state it. grpo_judge_max_calls has no default. After the dataset loads and before the model does, soup train (and soup train --dry-run) counts the calls the run could make, (train rows x epochs + held-out rows x evaluations) x 2 for the one retry of an unreadable reply, and refuses the run with exit 1 and a Judge budget: line naming the value to raise it to. Held-out rows count only when training.eval_steps is set. Inside each counted call a 429, a 5xx, a timeout or a lost connection is retried up to twice, so the judge host can see up to three requests per counted call.
  • A group the judge failed on scores nothing, not zero. A reply that is not a JSON object with one score in [0, 1] per completion is asked for once more. A group that still has no scores gets no reward and no advantage. The run logs judge/failed_group_rate and judge/equal_score_group_rate (groups whose completions all scored the same), and stops with an error naming the judge once more than grpo_judge_max_failure_rate of at least 20 training groups failed. A judge that cannot be reached ends the run.
  • Refused when the config loads: judge_rank on any task but grpo, on backend: mlx, with modality: vision (the judge would see the text and never the images), beside training.prm_reward (which replaces reward_fn) or training.rollout_backend (which replaces the prompts the budget counted); judge_rank without grpo_judge or grpo_judge_max_calls; and a grpo_judge* key without judge_rank in reward_fn. Refused when the trainer is set up: more than one process (WORLD_SIZE above 1), because each would judge only its own slice and keep its own failure count.

The policy learns to please the judge, not to be right, so read samples while it trains and keep a held-out check with a different judge or a person. Every new judge_rank field is off by default. No quality, speed or cost figure is claimed for judge_rank. (Separately, since v0.77.0 training.gradient_checkpointing reaches the GRPO trainer: with the default false a task: grpo run trains with checkpointing off, where TRL's own default used to apply, so set training.gradient_checkpointing: true, as the example above does, to keep the memory you had.)

Long-context & vision GRPO

blocks.code:
task: grpo
training:
  vllm_sleep_mode: true     # free vLLM memory between rollouts

blocks.html:
long_context_grpo and vision_grpo are validation gates, not features: they check the task, the backend and, for vision, a known VLM base (and the vision modality), and nothing reads them afterwards. long_context_grpo does not extend rope scaling into rollouts, and no Tiled MLP code stands behind it. vision_grpo does not make GRPO multimodal: the GRPO trainer loads the base with AutoModelForCausalLM and a tokenizer, not a vision processor. Both are on the list of 31 staged fields that are validated and read by nothing, and since v0.77.0 they stop the load when set away from their default: training.long_context_grpo is accepted but read by nothing; refused as of v0.77. Delete the line. (soup train exits 1, soup doctor --config exits 2). An explicit false still loads. In v0.76 they only warned. Deleting the line changes nothing about what trains. vllm_sleep_mode is read by the GRPO trainer.

Async rollout backends

blocks.code:
task: grpo
training:
  rollout_backend: openenv   # art | ruler | nemo_gym | openenv
  rollout_func: soup_cli.envs.calculator:rollout   # required by openenv

blocks.html:
openenv is the only backend that runs at v0.77.0. rollout_func is a module:function that receives the dataset prompts as seeds and returns the rows GRPO then trains on, which replace the dataset's prompts. It is not given the model and runs no interactive multi-turn episodes; the bundled soup_cli.envs.calculator:rollout is a single-shot seeder (see PRM-guided GRPO). art (OpenPipe ART), ruler (OpenPipe RULER, which ships inside openpipe-art) and nemo_gym are accepted names whose adapters are not wired: they raise an ImportError naming the missing package (openpipe-art for both art and ruler, nemo-gym for nemo_gym), and a "not yet validated" error when it is installed. Through v0.76.1 ruler named a package that is not on PyPI and counted PyPI's unrelated ruler package as installed (#2059). A rollout_backend cannot be combined with reward_fn: judge_rank (see judge_rank above).

Stability knobs (accepted; mostly record-only)

blocks.code:
task: grpo
training:
  ref_model_ema_alpha: 0.99   # EMA-style ref refresh
  replay_buffer_size: 50000
  tis_threshold: 1.5          # truncated importance sampling
  mask_truncated_completions: true
  defer_rerolling: true
  skip_zero_advantage: true
  off_policy_mask_threshold: 0.7
  async_grpo_prefetch: true

blocks.html:
At v0.77.0 these eight keys are accepted for task: grpo and attach a callback that writes counters (replay_size, tis_alerts, ema_alpha) into the training log. The one thing that callback does to training is the gradient watchdog described above, which skips non-finite optimizer steps and is attached to every task: grpo run, with or without these keys. async_grpo_prefetch, mask_truncated_completions, defer_rerolling, skip_zero_advantage and off_policy_mask_threshold do not change what the trainer does: the callback's own notes call them advisory, a hint or record-only. The replay buffer is never fed and the TIS counter is never called. ref_model_ema_alpha can only act if the callback is handed a separate reference model, and the Hugging Face callback handler does not hand it one, so there is nothing for it to update; a LoRA run has no separate reference model anyway (read from the code, not run on a GPU). These eight keys are not among the 31 staged fields that v0.77.0 refuses at load, so they load without a message. What does work on this page: the seven grpo_variant objectives (with the grpo_beta KL penalty on the six non-standard ones), grpo_delta, grpo_fp16, vllm_sleep_mode and the openenv rollout.

New task: prm

task: prm (Process Reward Model) wired through the standard reward-model trainer. Gates: vision + GRPO compat checked.

v0.50.0 shipped the schema. v0.53.3 wired grpo_fp16 routing + the known-VLM-base gate for vision_grpo; v0.53.11 lit up real loss kernels for every non-standard variant (gspo / dapo / dr_grpo / bnpo / two_sided / rft) via make_grpo_trainer_variant, made task: prm live with per-step MSE + reward head, and attached GRPOStabilityCallback, which logs counters for the stability knobs above (most of them are record-only, as that section says). See v0.53.11 — GRPO Plus finish.
